Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Please keep the units beside the quantities in the working sheet, since a case, a carton, and an individual item do not mean the same thing for ordering.

The North Street cooler contained 43 tubs of plain yogurt, each 500 grams, and 31 tubs of cultured butter, each 250 grams. One yogurt tub was open when the count was made, so it was entered among the 43 but marked for staff review rather than for sale. No decision about that tub is recorded in this review. The thermometer reading written on the cooler log at 7:42 a.m. was 4.2°C. The East Annex had 52 cartons of oat milk and 18 cases of canned tomatoes. Those amounts are separate from the North Street figures and should not be added into a store-level total without a location label. The Annex count was supplied by Imani at 8:10 a.m. by phone, rather than taken by the North Street counting team. Imani said, “The back row is clear now, and I checked the date labels before I called.” Her call confirmed the listed stock in that room, but it did not include a count of the freezer or the small locked cupboard beside the loading door. Those areas are outside this review, so leave their quantities blank rather than treating them as zero.

The receiving notebook records 24 cartons of oat milk and 10 cases of tomatoes delivered to North Street on Monday. These are receipts during the review period, not additional units on top of the counted closing stock. The oat milk cartons were already included in the 186-carton count, and the tomato cases were already included in the 16-case count. The opening balance for lentils was not copied into the notebook, so the review cannot use the receipt and issue notes to calculate a complete period balance.

For the spreadsheet handoff, use the filename below for the export that carries the location, product, counted quantity, unit, and note fields. The name is already used by the cooperative’s shared folder, so keep its spelling and punctuation unchanged.
delivery-summary.tsv
The export should show the North Street and East Annex rows separately. Put the 12 wet-packaging oat milk cartons in a note field while retaining them within the North Street count of 186 cartons. Likewise, retain the community-kitchen apples within the 28-crate total and identify the 4-crate allocation in the note field. Do not turn the 4 crates into a second quantity. The export is intended for the receiving and packing teams, not as a substitute for the temperature log or the receiving notebook.

1. Before the next order is prepared, compare the shelf count for each listed product with the quantity on the order worksheet. Record a difference only after checking the product name, location, and unit. A difference of 1 case is not the same as a difference of 1 can, and the tomato case count must remain in cases until the pack size is applied. If a label is unreadable, write “label check needed” in the note field and leave the counted quantity as recorded; the label should not be guessed from a neighboring shelf.
2. Keep exceptions attached to the relevant line. The open yogurt tub belongs with the North Street yogurt entry and should retain its staff-review note. The wet cartons belong with North Street oat milk. The 6 lentil bags issued to the kitchen belong in the movement notes, not in the current count. These details affect how the next shift interprets the numbers, even though they do not change the counted totals given above.
3. Ask the shift lead to confirm the later cooler log before dairy is dispatched. The hold instruction applies only if the recorded temperature is above 5°C for at least 20 minutes; if that condition is not recorded, this review does not itself call for a hold. Keep the time and reading from any later log with the dairy dispatch record, rather than changing the morning reading of 4.2°C.
